chunks: Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): I debated a group and said to them: Indeed Allah, Majestic is His Majesty, is more Majestic, more Mighty, and more Benevolent than that He should be recognized through His creation; rather, it is the servants who are recognized through Allah. So he said: May Allah have mercy on you.

key_terms.الْعِبَادُ يُعْرَفُونَ بِاللَّهِ: the servants are recognized through Allah — the correct theological position: God is the primary reality through which all else is known
key_terms.جَلَّ جَلَالُهُ: Majestic is His Majesty — a formula of divine glorification (azwj), affirming God's absolute transcendence
key_terms.يُعْرَفَ بِخَلْقِهِ: to be recognized through His creation — the erroneous approach, treating creation as a prior epistemic lens for knowing God

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq explain how God is known — through creation or through Himself?
ai.summary: In this celebrated theological report, Mansur ibn Hazim narrates a key exchange with Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) in which he describes an argument he presented to a group during a theological debate. Mansur asserted that God transcends being known through His creatures — the relationship is inverted: creatures are known through God, not the other way around. The Imam's brief but powerful response, 'May Allah have mercy on you,' constitutes an endorsement of this argument. This hadith is foundational to the Shia theology of divine transcendence (tanzih) and the epistemological priority of God over creation.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on you

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazan, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Mansour Bin Hazim who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I debated a group, so I said to them that Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Majestic is His<sup>azwj</sup> Majesty is more Majestic and more Mighty, and more Benevolent than that He<sup>azwj</sup> should be recognised through His<sup>azwj</sup> creatures. en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Isma‘il has narrated the following from al-Fadl ibn shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim who has said that

I spoke to Imam abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) saying, “I debated certain people and said to them, ‘Allah, Glory be to Him, is far Glorious, Majestic and Honorable than being defined by means of His creatures. In fact, the existence of the creatures is proved through the existence of Allah.’” The Imam (a.s.) said, “May Allah bestow up on you blessings.”
